metadata.description: ether.fi is a liquid staking and restaking protocol where users deposit ETH into the LiquidityPool and receive eETH, a rebasing receipt token with a market capitalization of $5.64B. Deposited ETH is used to provision Ethereum validators through the StakingManager and EtherFiNodesManager, which run validators via EigenLayer EigenPods, and idle liquidity is restaked through EigenLayer strategies and Lido stETH by the EtherFiRestaker. Upgrades and protocol-wide changes route through a 10-day TimelockController controlled by a 6-of-10 multisig, while a separate 2-day operational timelock, a 4-of-7 operations multisig, and several EOAs hold lower-tier roles for validator operations, parameter tuning, and pausing. The protocol relies on EigenLayer for restaking, Lido for stETH withdrawals, and LayerZero for cross-chain messaging.

admins.name: StakingManager
admins.description: Protocol-internal contract that owns the UpgradeableBeacon backing all EtherFiNode instances, so it can upgrade the implementation used by every node. It also handles validator key linking, auction settlement, and EigenPod creation. Its own owner is the EtherFi Timelock, so external control traces back to the governance multisig.

admins.name: EtherFi Governance Multisig (6-of-10)
admins.description: Gnosis Safe holding the PROPOSER, EXECUTOR and CANCELLER roles on the 10-day EtherFi Timelock. It is the sole entity able to schedule, execute and cancel timelock operations, so it effectively controls every contract the timelock owns ($0 in reachable capital), with all changes gated behind the 10-day delay.

admins.name: EtherFi Timelock (10-day delay)
admins.description: OpenZeppelin TimelockController that directly owns 42 protocol contracts, controlling $0 in capital and $0 in eETH token value. It can upgrade every core contract (LiquidityPool, StakingManager, EtherFiNodesManager, WithdrawRequestNFT, MembershipManager, EtherFiOracle and others), grant and revoke RoleRegistry roles, change fee and rate parameters, and move funds via withdraw and sweep functions. All actions are subject to a 10-day (864000-second) minimum delay before execution.

admins.name: EtherfiL1SyncPoolETH
admins.description: Protocol-internal contract that mints eETH against cross-chain deposits bridged via LayerZero and unwraps L2 ETH. Its proxy is upgradeable by the EtherFi Operations Multisig (4-of-7) without timelock delay.

admins.name: Zero Address (Renounced)
admins.description: Several contract permissions point to the zero address, meaning those ownership or minter roles have been renounced and can no longer be exercised.

admins.name: EtherFi Operations Multisig (4-of-7)
admins.description: Gnosis Safe holding broad operating-admin roles — EETH_OPERATING_ADMIN_ROLE, STAKING_MANAGER_ADMIN_ROLE, ETHERFI_RATE_LIMITER_ADMIN_ROLE, PRIORITY_WITHDRAWAL_QUEUE_ADMIN_ROLE, plus PROTOCOL_PAUSER and PROTOCOL_UNPAUSER. It also owns the ProxyAdmin contracts that upgrade the EtherfiL1SyncPoolETH cross-chain contract without timelock delay. Ownership and the LayerZero messaging delegate of the EtherfiOFTAdapterUpgradeable — which configures LayerZero peers and rate limits for cross-chain eETH bridging — were transferred to the EtherFi operational timelock (2-day delay) in June 2026, so those changes now carry a 2-day delay rather than executing instantly through this multisig. Direct capital exposure is $0.

admins.name: EtherFi Operational Timelock (2-day delay)
admins.description: A second TimelockController with a 2-day (172800-second) delay holding operational RoleRegistry roles — LIQUIDITY_POOL_ADMIN_ROLE, ETHERFI_REDEMPTION_MANAGER_ADMIN_ROLE, ETHERFI_NODES_MANAGER_ADMIN_ROLE, ETHERFI_ORACLE_EXECUTOR_ADMIN_ROLE and others. It tunes redemption parameters (exit fees, capacity, refill rate), registers validator spawners, manages EigenPod operations, and queues withdrawals, with $0 in direct capital exposure. Its EtherFiNodesManager call-forwarding allowlist is currently limited to EigenLayer delegation management (delegateTo, redelegate, undelegate).

dependencies.name: Ethereum Beacon Chain Deposit Contract
dependencies.description: The canonical Ethereum staking deposit contract. ether.fi calls deposit on it when funding new validators through createBeaconValidators and confirmAndFundBeaconValidators.

dependencies.name: EigenPodManager (EigenLayer)
dependencies.description: EigenLayer contract that deploys and manages EigenPods. ether.fi creates one EigenPod per validator node and routes validator creation, checkpoint proofs, consolidations and execution-layer withdrawals through it.

dependencies.name: LayerZero EndpointV2
dependencies.description: The LayerZero V2 messaging endpoint. ether.fi uses it to send and receive cross-chain messages for the L1 sync pool and OFT token bridging, and to set its messaging delegate.

dependencies.name: LayerZero ReceiveUln302
dependencies.description: LayerZero's receive-side message library defining the validation of inbound cross-chain messages for the protocol's cross-chain components.

dependencies.name: LayerZero Endpoint Owner
dependencies.description: The owner of the LayerZero EndpointV2 and its Send/Receive message libraries. It can register libraries and change the default send and receive libraries used for cross-chain verification, which the protocol's cross-chain messaging depends on.

dependencies.name: DelegationManager (EigenLayer)
dependencies.description: EigenLayer contract managing operator delegations and withdrawals. ether.fi delegates restaked positions, queues and completes withdrawals through it; $0 in capital flows depend on it.

dependencies.name: StrategyManager (EigenLayer)
dependencies.description: EigenLayer contract that accepts deposits into restaking strategies. The EtherFiRestaker calls depositIntoStrategy on it to restake liquid staking tokens.

dependencies.name: Lido WithdrawalQueueERC721
dependencies.description: Lido's withdrawal queue contract. ether.fi requests and claims stETH withdrawals through it via stEthRequestWithdrawal and stEthClaimWithdrawals.

dependencies.name: RewardsCoordinator (EigenLayer)
dependencies.description: EigenLayer contract distributing restaking rewards. ether.fi sets a rewards claimer on it via setClaimerFor so restaking rewards can be claimed on the protocol's behalf.

dependencies.name: Lido stETH
dependencies.description: Lido's staked ETH token. ether.fi holds and transfers stETH through the EtherFiRestaker and Liquifier, and supports redeeming eETH/weETH against stETH balances.

dependencies.name: Coinbase cbETH
dependencies.description: Coinbase's wrapped staked ETH token, accepted as a deposit asset. Its exchange rate is read by the protocol when valuing cbETH deposits.

dependencies.name: Curve WrapTokenV3ETH
dependencies.description: A Curve-related wrapped ETH token accepted as a deposit asset; the protocol reads its exchange rate and total supply and routes deposits through the EtherFiRestaker.

dependencies.name: Curve Pool
dependencies.description: A Curve pool used by the protocol to quote and execute swaps between deposit assets; the protocol calls get_dy on it during depositWithERC20 flows.

funds.name: LiquidityPool (ETH)
funds.description: Holds $25.46M, almost entirely unstaked ETH awaiting deployment into validators or redemption. This is the protocol's main liquidity buffer.

funds.name: EtherFiRestaker (Restaking positions)
funds.description: Holds $1.32B in restaking positions, predominantly ETH staked through Lido with a smaller EigenLayer position. This contract restakes idle protocol liquidity to generate additional yield.

funds.name: eETH Token
funds.description: The protocol's rebasing liquid staking token, with a circulating market capitalization of $5.64B. eETH represents a user's claim on staked ETH plus accrued staking and restaking rewards.

funds.name: Treasury (ETH)
funds.description: Holds $24.62K in ETH, accumulating protocol fees and revenue. It is owned by the EtherFi Timelock.

changes.before: The DelegationManager contract is responsible for registering EigenLayer operators and managing the EigenLayer strategies delegations. The EigenDA StakeRegistry contract reads from the DelegationManager to track the total stake of each EigenDA operator.

governance.votingProcess: Snapshot vote (4-day window, 1M ETHFI quorum). Foundation multisig executes the proposals arbitrarily
